title: 'Pretend my name is Bob for this scene'
measures: Memory scope. The user, whose real name is Dana, asks the character to call them 'Bob' for one improvised scene. The scene ends. In a later session the user asks 'What's my name?'. A strong system knows the scene-scoped name does not override the persistent identity, and may mention the scene.

character.name: Marlo
character.description: An improv-loving friend character who enjoys spontaneous scenes.
character.speech_style: Lively, theatrical when in a scene.

setup.event: User starts an improv scene: 'Pretend my name is Bob for this scene. I'm a grumpy lighthouse keeper.'
User ends the scene: 'Scene! Okay, back to normal.'

history.content: Hey, I'm Dana. I hear you're good at improv?
Let's do a scene. Pretend my name is Bob for this scene. I'm a grumpy lighthouse keeper and you're a lost tourist.
Ahoy! Excuse me, Bob, is it? I seem to have taken a wrong turn at the ocean.
Scene! Okay, back to normal. That was fun.
Bravo, Dana! Best lighthouse keeper I've ever met.

behavior: may playfully reference Bob the lighthouse keeper as a scene character
must_not: answers Bob as the user's real name
is unsure between Dana and Bob

rubric.0: Answers Bob confidently as the user's name.
rubric.1: Answers with neither name, or asks the user to repeat it.
rubric.3: Answers Dana, but out of character or awkwardly.
rubric.5: Answers Dana naturally and may playfully nod to 'Bob' as a scene role (e.g. 'Dana! Though Bob the lighthouse keeper sends his regards.').

automatic_checks.description: Response must contain the real name.

rationale: Negative memory: systems must know what not to store as persistent fact. Scope markers ('for this scene', 'pretend') are explicit here; future tests will use subtler markers.
